title: Tortilla chips
question: How do you pick tortilla chips?
decision: Tortilla chips from corn cooked the traditional way, in limewater.
why: Corn cooked in limewater grinds into masa, a dough. Untreated cornmeal will not form one.
short_answer: Corn for tortillas is cooked in an alkaline solution, usually limewater, then ground into masa. Some corn chips use corn that never went through that step. Masa and a trace of lime often show on the ingredients.
detail: The step is nixtamalization: dry corn is soaked and cooked in a solution of slaked lime and water. Slaked lime is calcium hydroxide, called “cal.” The cooked corn, called nixtamal, is washed, then ground into a dough, masa. The word comes from Nahuatl, the Aztec language. Cornmeal from untreated corn cannot form a dough with water alone. Masa harina means “dough flour,” the powder ground from nixtamal. Masa flour made at scale is based on the traditional method. Restaurant-style chips are tortillas cut into wedges and fried. Most bagged chips are shaped straight from coarse masa dough and fried.
kristy_take: Traditionally, the corn soaks overnight in lime and water, is rinsed and rubbed free of its hulls, then ground on a flat lava stone. The practice began in Mesoamerica, where the earliest equipment dates from 1200 to 1500 BCE. In parts of the region, the old techniques persist.
buying_tips: Read the ingredients for masa or corn masa.
A trace of lime on the list points to the traditional cooking step.
“Restaurant-style” chips are tortillas cut into wedges and fried.
watch_out: Some corn chips are made from corn that was never cooked in lime.

labels_decoded.meaning: A dough ground from corn that was cooked in an alkaline solution.
On a chip list, the alkali the corn was cooked in, not the citrus fruit.
A name sometimes used for chips made from corn that was never lime-cooked.

tier_note: Masa on the ingredients means the corn was cooked first.
